title: CFG-proxy + tokenizer-boundary guardrails for structured-output backends
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: production structured-output customers hit two classes of failures: (1) CFG-backed decoders that produce valid parse trees in token-space but violate tokenizer boundary assumptions (truncated symbols, split escape sequences) causing downstream parsers to fail; (2) streaming sessions where intermediate chunking breaks grammar enforcement and yields unparsable partial frames. This PR introduces a thin CFG-proxy layer that normalizes grammar outputs to tokenizer-safe symbol boundaries and a set of guardrails to make grammar and regex backends robust in streaming and OpenAI-compat scenarios.

What this changes: 
- CFG-proxy service (runtime shim): normalizes nonterminal emission points to token boundaries by post-processing logits and applying a small resampling/fallback loop when boundary heuristics detect splits. The proxy lives alongside existing sampling backends and is feature-flagged.
- Boundary heuristics: tokenizer-aware checks that detect incomplete UTF sequences, split escape tokens, and partial punctuation tokens; these trigger conservative backoffs or a switch to regex backend to avoid producing invalid structured payloads.
- Streaming resilience: streaming frame decoder now tracks tokenization cut points and emits explicit "partial-frame" markers to the client-side framing shim; serverside decoder will attempt to complete frames up to a configurable window before falling back. This reduces noisy parse failures during long-running streams.
- Backend orchestration: new backend_priority config for structured-output routes. Defaults: [CFG-proxy, regex, sampling]. Operators can reorder via route config.
- OpenAI-compat improvements: function-calling shim now validates that arguments satisfy tokenizer-boundary constraints before returning; if validation fails, we include a single repair attempt using the proxy and mark the call with metadata compatible with the OpenAI compatibility layer.
- Metrics & observability: added structured_output.parse_success, structured_output.fallback_count, structured_output.proxy_latency, and a synthetic "partial_frame_rate" metric to identify streaming fragmentation. Dashboards updated in observability-pack.
- Tests: unit tests for tokenizer heuristics, e2e test harness that runs a mini streaming session against the proxy + regex fallback, and fuzzer cases for common edge tokens (emoji, multi-byte punctuation, escape sequences).

How it works (high level): the CFG-proxy accepts logits or candidate token sequences from the CFG backend, runs tokenizer boundary analysis, and either (a) accepts and re-encodes the sequence, (b) nudges sampling at the next step to resolve a boundary, or (c) delegates to regex backend with a signed context blob when heuristics are uncertain. We intentionally keep the proxy logic small and auditable to avoid altering model behavior more than necessary.

Backward compatibility & rollout: rollout is gated behind a per-route feature flag (structured_output.cfg_proxy_enabled). We deployed in canary for 48h on customers using structured-output routes; observed parse_success +6.8% and fallback_count ~0.9% on first-pass repairs. No customer-facing schema changes. The OpenAI-compat shim only adds metadata to responses when repair logic ran.

Risk mitigation: revert keypaths added to runtime config are simple toggles. Proxy is CPU-light (string-level ops) and can be disabled per-route. We added a synthetic low-latency path for tail-latency sensitive routes that bypasses proxy but keeps a conservative regex gate.

Testing & validation: CI includes unit and integration tests. Performed a small staged rollout across Dedicated and hosted fleets. Observability alerts added to detect regressions in latency and parse_success.

Related links: ENG-1984 (root cause analysis), ENG-2051 (streaming framing incidents), internal RFC: rfc/structured-output-cfg-proxy.md
commits: initial: add cfg-proxy shim and API hooks
runtime: tokenizer-boundary heuristics and unit tests
streaming: partial-frame markers + framing shim adjustments
orchestration: backend_priority config and route flag
patch_snippets:
--- a/runtimes/structured_output/tokenizer_guardrails.py
+++ b/runtimes/structured_output/tokenizer_guardrails.py
@@ def detect_split_token(seq, tokenizer):
-    return any(partial for partial in tokenizer.split(seq))
+    # ensure we treat multi-byte and escape sequences as atomic units
+    toks = tokenizer.tokenize(seq)
+    return any(t.endswith('@@') or t.startswith('@@') for t in toks)
discussion: Diego Morales (reviewer): I like the proxy approach. Two asks: add a flag to disable the regex fallback per-tenant and add more comments in the proxy explaining the failure modes.
Ava Chen (author): Added per-tenant toggle at routemgr and expanded inline docs. PTAL.
Samir Patel (reviewer): We should ensure the proxy can't amplify hallucinations by repeatedly nudging the model. Please add a rate limit on repair attempts.
Ava Chen (author): Added a repair_attempts_window and hard cap in the proxy. Also added metric structured_output.repair_rate to track this.
Lina Park (approver): Tests look solid. Observability names are clear. Approving for merge after CI green and a brief load test.
release_notes: Add optional CFG-proxy shim that normalizes grammar outputs to tokenizer-safe boundaries, improves streaming structured-output reliability, and introduces regex fallback with observability. Feature-flagged per route.
